policyAvailabilityDependencies.description: Parent/child availability model for Power Pages authentication governance. A portal (or the whole environment) is only ELIGIBLE ('available') for a CHILD policy's governance setting when EVERY parent listed in that child's `availabilityDependsOn` is Enabled for that portal/env. When a gating parent is Disabled for a portal/env, the portal is UNAVAILABLE for the child policy: it cannot be enabled or disabled there and must be shown in the picker BELOW the available portals with the blocking parent named. This mirrors the product rule that a specific sign-in method can only be governed on a portal where its umbrella provider is turned on. `EnableExternalAuthProviders` is the root parent (the Main Flag) of the four sign-in protocols; `EnableProtocolOpenAuth` (OAuth 2.0) is in turn the parent of the three OAuth-based social identity providers. Each dependent policy carries the same list in its own `availabilityDependsOn` field — the per-policy field is what the resolver reads; this block is the readable overview / single source of truth for the tree shape.
policyAvailabilityDependencies.unknownParentPostureNote: When a parent's live state cannot be read (network/parse failure), the portal is treated as AVAILABLE (fail-open) so a transient read error never hides portals from the admin. The resolver annotates such portals so the orchestrator can note the unread parent rather than silently blocking.

effectiveStatusRules.description: How the EFFECTIVE (real, end-user-observable) status of a child sign-in method is computed for the status-display paths (Fetch Env portal table, Fetch Site, and the post-Set verify table). A child method's own governance setting being Enabled is necessary but NOT sufficient: the method only actually works on a portal when EVERY gating parent (the transitive `availabilityDependsOn` chain) is also Enabled on that portal. This mirrors the product runtime — e.g. Google sign-in is dark on a portal where OAuth 2.0 or External Auth is off even if the Google setting itself is Enabled, because the umbrella provider gates it. The status tables therefore show the child's own state PLUS a column for each parent, and an Effective column = own AND all parents. The parent columns to display are exactly the child's `availabilityDependsOn` list, in order (External Auth first, then OAuth 2.0 for social IdPs).
effectiveStatusRules.effectiveRule: effective = Enabled iff (ownState == Enabled) AND every parent in availabilityDependsOn is Enabled for that portal; Disabled iff no state is Unknown and at least one of {own, ...parents} is Disabled; otherwise Unknown (a parent or own state could not be read).
effectiveStatusRules.note: `parentColumnsByPolicy` is the readable overview; the renderer reads each child's own `availabilityDependsOn` field (authoritative). Policies absent here (Maker Copilot, local login, and External Auth itself as a root) have no parents — their effective status equals their own state and no parent columns render.

stateColors.description: Color convention for rendering Governance Setting state in summary/verification/state tables. The Status column is wrapped in ANSI SGR codes so it renders green/red in an ANSI-capable terminal; the emoji marker is kept as a fallback indicator for surfaces that strip ANSI (e.g. some chat renderers). Wrap the whole Status cell as `<ansi><emoji> <label> (<paraphrase>)<reset>`.
